name: Nyadu
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: One last possible predictor for the distribution of prestopped nasals might be suprasegmental. This is not plausible, however, as Banyaduq has neither contrastive stress nor tone. It is beyond the purview of this paper to discuss whether Banyaduq has stress at all, but descriptively, final vowels are consistently pronounced with slightly higher duration and intensity. For example, the final [u] is prominent in both (25b) [ŋãrum] ‘night’ and (23c) [mõrupm] ‘to fly.’ Stress cannot, then, provide an explanation for why only the latter has a prestopped nasal.
new_statements.citation: Jardine, Adam, Angeliki Athanasopoulou, Kristian & Peter Cole. 2015. Banyaduq prestopped nasals: Synchrony and diachrony. Oceanic Linguistics 54(2): 548-578. doi:10.1353/ol.2015.0018 (quoted from the author's accepted manuscript, Aug 2015).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is not contrastive (and there is no tone); to the extent there is word-level prominence it is on the final syllable: word-final vowels are consistently realized with somewhat greater duration and intensity. The authors explicitly leave open whether this final prominence should be called 'stress'.
new_statements.exceptions: None; final-vowel prominence described as consistent across words (illustrated with [ŋãrum] 'night' and [mõrupm] 'to fly').
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level, based on elicited citation forms from fieldwork on the Sangke village dialect (native-speaker co-author Kristian); impressionistic ('descriptively'), not an instrumental stress study; the paper's topic is prestopped nasals and the stress remark is made in passing to rule out a suprasegmental conditioning factor.
new_statements.identity_note: nyad1241 'Nyadu' [nxj] is a Glottolog Bookkeeping languoid: ISO 639-3 Change Request 2007-255 (Peebles & Anderbeck, SIL; adopted 2008-01-14) retired [nxj] and merged it into [byd] Benyadu' on Collins's judgement that 'Nyadu is the same language as Benyadu''. The living languoid is Glottolog beny1237 Benyadu' (Banyaduq, Banyadu, Balantian; Land Dayak/Bidayuhic, Landak and Bengkayang regencies, West Kalimantan), which is a separate NO-SOURCE-FOUND target in WORLD_TARGETS. The quoted source describes the Sangke-village dialect of Banyaduq (southern Banyaduq area, Landak Regency); the statement should be catalogued under beny1237, with nyad1241 pointing to it.
